question: Why does a Quality Assurance Committee need members from different departments (multidisciplinary)?

options.A: To make committee meetings last longer
options.B: To reduce the number of doctors needed in the wards
options.C: Because government laws forbid single-profession committees
options.D: Because patient care involves many different health professionals working together

explanation: Spot on! Since nursing, pharmacy, and medicine all work together for the patient, everyone needs a voice on the team. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h2)

question: Nursing informatics brings together which three main fields?

options.A: It requires a degree in computer engineering and clinical medicine.
options.B: It combines computer science, information science, and nursing science.
options.C: It replaces traditional bedside nursing care with automated machines.
options.D: It focuses exclusively on repairing broken hospital computer hardware.

explanation: You don't need to be a tech wizard! Nursing informatics simply blends tech tools with nursing knowledge to make patient care smoother. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing duty under the Mother-Baby Package?

options.A: Educating mothers on exclusive breastfeeding practices
options.B: Conducting routine antenatal assessments and checkups
options.C: Administering childhood immunizations according to the schedule
options.D: Performing elective major surgeries in primary health clinics

explanation: Correct! Major surgeries belong in a surgical theater with a doctor, not at a basic primary health clinic. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h7)

question: A nurse needs to check a patient's lab results from three days ago during an emergency. What is the primary operational advantage of using an EHR in this situation?

options.A: Automatic notification sent to the hospital director
options.B: Instant retrieval of past records without searching physical files
options.C: Immediate permission to discharge the patient home
options.D: Free medical insurance coverage for the laboratory test

explanation: Digital archiving allows clinicians to pull up historical lab data in seconds, supporting faster and safer emergency decisions. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h5)

question: What happens to a DRF if hospital staff constantly collect drugs on credit and fail to pay back?

options.A: The suppliers will double the credit period for future orders
options.B: The pharmacy will automatically start generating higher profits
options.C: The fund will quickly experience cash depletion and stockouts
options.D: The government will automatically inject fresh emergency funds

explanation: Unpaid credit creates holes in the system. If the cash doesn't come back in, the pharmacy won't have money to buy new medicines when patients need them. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is a common sign of compassion fatigue in disaster nurses?

options.A: Emotional numbness, irritability, and burnout
options.B: Increased energy and enthusiasm for work
options.C: Complete indifference to physical illnesses
options.D: An intense desire to work double shifts daily

explanation: Absorbing too much trauma without adequate recovery leads to emotional exhaustion and classic signs of burnout. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h8)

question: Why is it important to involve men and community leaders in safe motherhood programs?

options.A: They are the only ones allowed inside antenatal care wards
options.B: They are trained to perform emergency caesarean sections
options.C: They often control household finances and transportation decisions
options.D: They replace the need for professional nurses in the village

explanation: In many settings, men hold the decision-making power regarding money and travel, making their buy-in crucial for emergency care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h7)

question: What is the main difference between quarantine and isolation?

options.A: Quarantine restricts people who were exposed but are not yet sick, while isolation separates those who are already confirmed sick.
options.B: Quarantine involves giving preventive medications, while isolation involves performing major surgical procedures.
options.C: Quarantine is only used for waterborne diseases, whereas isolation is reserved exclusively for vector-borne illnesses.
options.D: Quarantine takes place in private homes, while isolation can only happen in national research laboratories.

explanation: Easy way to remember: Isolation is for those who are already sick, while quarantine is for those who were exposed and are waiting to see if they fall ill. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T85#GNS214_U1_T85_h5)

question: How does the skin act as a blood reservoir during strenuous exercise?

options.A: Sweat glands pull extra blood out through the pores
options.B: Subcutaneous fat pumps blood back to the heart
options.C: The epidermis stores extra blood cells in dead layers
options.D: Dermal vessels constrict to send blood to active muscles

explanation: Constricting blood vessels in the skin shifts stored blood toward exercising muscles and vital organs. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h7)

question: Why might a nurse manager sometimes fail to use the most theoretically perfect solution to a problem?

options.A: Theory never has any connection to real-world nursing
options.B: Hospital policy forbids the use of logic in management
options.C: Staff members always refuse to do any work at all
options.D: Power dynamics and institutional policies create practical limits

explanation: In the real hospital environment, politics, hospital policies, and power struggles often force managers to find practical compromises. [learn more](GST321_U1_T8#GST321_U1_T8_h5)

question: What does the 'double burden of malnutrition' mean in growing cities?

options.A: Suffering from two different strains of malaria at once
options.B: Having to pay double the price for imported rice
options.C: The presence of both childhood stunting and adult obesity
options.D: Carrying heavy water buckets over long distances

explanation: City environments can sometimes show both sides of the coin: undernutrition in young children and weight-related health issues in adults. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T022#GNS227_U2_T022_h5)

question: Why can't a nurse just focus on pure biology (like lab tests and vitals) when caring for a mental health patient?

options.A: Psychological symptoms have no connection to physical health at all
options.B: External life events and social pressures deeply affect emotional well-being
options.C: Doctors rarely pay attention to physical lab results during admission
options.D: Biological tests are too expensive to run in most local clinics

explanation: You got it! A patient's daily struggles, relationships, and environment heavily shape their mental health. We treat the whole person, not just the lab results. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T2#GNS314_U6_T2_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common consequence of relying solely on a free market for healthcare?

options.A: Universal and equal access for all citizens regardless of wealth
options.B: Neglect of unprofitable public health services
options.C: Lack of basic care for uninsured populations
options.D: Geographic concentration of hospitals in wealthy urban areas

explanation: A pure free market distributes care based on ability to pay, which naturally creates disparities rather than universal equal access. [learn more](GST322_U1_T4#GST322_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why is follow-up care considered essential for patients with chronic mental health conditions?

options.A: Patients no longer need family support once they leave the ward
options.B: Mental illnesses often require long-term monitoring to prevent symptom return
options.C: Community clinics have unlimited space for permanent admissions
options.D: Discharge medications are designed to cure the illness permanently

explanation: Because chronic mental health conditions fluctuate over time, ongoing care helps catch early changes before a full relapse occurs. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h1)

question: What does a pulse oximeter measure in a patient?

options.A: Blood oxygen saturation levels
options.B: Electrical activity of the heart
options.C: Arterial blood pressure
options.D: Internal core body temperature

explanation: A pulse oximeter shines light through the skin to calculate how much oxygen is carried by the red blood cells. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why is knowing the location of the dorsal penile nerves important during a circumcision?

options.A: It controls the blood flow to the entire lower abdomen
options.B: It guides where to give a local nerve block for pain relief
options.C: It helps prevent accidental removal of the urethral opening
options.D: It ensures the scrotal skin heals without any scarring

explanation: You've got this! Doctors inject local numbing medication near these dorsal nerves on top of the penis to block pain signals effectively and keep the baby comfortable. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T5#GNS311_U4_T5_h2)

question: What is the correct way to fix a writing mistake on a paper patient chart?

options.A: Use liquid correction fluid to completely hide the word
options.B: Draw a single line through the error and initial it
options.C: Tear out the entire page and rewrite the whole note
options.D: Scribble over the mistake multiple times until it is black

explanation: A neat single line through the mistake keeps the original text readable while showing it was corrected, protecting the chart's legal status. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which of these is a common physical danger resulting from an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Rapid fetal bone growth
options.C: Uterine perforation and severe infection
options.D: Permanent high blood pressure

explanation: Correct! When procedures are done without proper training or sterile tools, it can easily tear the uterus and cause severe, life-threatening pelvic infections. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T014#GNS226_U1_T014_h3)

question: What is the best feeding item to use when giving ORS to an infant?

options.A: A clean cup and spoon
options.B: A rubber feeding bottle
options.C: A wide-spout drinking straw
options.D: A plastic syringe with a needle

explanation: Always choose a clean cup and spoon! Baby bottles have narrow parts that are very hard to clean properly and can easily trap germs that cause more infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h6)

question: During which stage of group development do members first experience friction and personality clashes?

options.A: Norming
options.B: Performing
options.C: Storming
options.D: Forming

explanation: The storming stage is marked by disagreements and tension as members push against boundaries and test each other's styles. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h2)

question: How can a growing economy help reduce the 'brain drain' of health professionals leaving Nigeria?

options.A: By providing competitive salaries and better working conditions locally
options.B: By making international travel passports illegal for nurses
options.C: By offering free housing in exchange for mandatory overtime
options.D: By forcing foreign hospitals to reject Nigerian applicants

explanation: If local pay and working conditions improve at home, nurses won't feel forced to look abroad for greener pastures. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h4)

question: When a patient is injured by a medical error, why do they often sue the hospital along with the nurse?

options.A: State laws forbid patients from ever suing a registered nurse directly
options.B: Individual nurses are completely immune from any civil lawsuits
options.C: Hospitals usually have greater financial resources to pay damages
options.D: Hospitals are legally required to commit the nurse to prison

explanation: Institutions have deeper pockets than individual nurses, making them a primary target when compensation is being sought for a mistake. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h1)

question: What is the main goal of destroying a disease reservoir?

options.A: To eliminate the environmental or animal habitat where the pathogen survives
options.B: To provide permanent immunity to all human members of an affected community
options.C: To increase the population of beneficial predators that feed on disease vectors
options.D: To chemically alter drinking water supplies so they taste better to locals

explanation: Exactly! By taking away their home or habitat, we cut off the source of the infection entirely. Smart thinking! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is a major goal of public awareness campaigns in disaster management?

options.A: To sell emergency preparedness gear to private businesses
options.B: To replace formal emergency services with untrained citizens
options.C: To collect data for national census and population records
options.D: To educate citizens on evacuation routes and local hazard risks

explanation: When people know what signs to look out for and where to run for safety, they can protect themselves long before help arrives. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h6)

question: What is the main cause of metabolic joint diseases?

options.A: Gradual loss of cartilage due to normal physical aging
options.B: Direct bacterial infection of the synovial fluid
options.C: Chemical imbalances and crystal deposits in the joints
options.D: Autoimmune attack triggered by environmental allergies

explanation: You've got this! These conditions happen when internal chemical errors cause crystals to build up in the joints, setting off painful inflammation. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h1)

question: Days after surviving a flood, a patient is restless, has a racing heart, and worries constantly. What is the best way to describe this?

options.A: Anxiety and panic
options.B: Depressive symptoms
options.C: Somatization
options.D: Acute stress reaction

explanation: Spot on! Constant worry, a restless body, and a fast heartbeat are classic signs of anxiety and panic following a scary crisis event. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T3#GNS314_U6_T3_h2)

question: Which type of waste must be burned at very high temperatures instead of just going into an autoclave?

options.A: Cardboard medication delivery boxes
options.B: Empty intravenous fluid plastic bags
options.C: Pathological waste and human tissues
options.D: Uncontaminated paper paperwork

explanation: Anatomical parts and human tissues require high-temperature incineration for safety and out of respect for human dignity. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h6)

question: What is a key everyday duty for health workers when it comes to food policy?

options.A: Writing the national budget for farm machinery
options.B: Designing state highways for food transport trucks
options.C: Conducting infant growth monitoring to spot early signs of malnutrition
options.D: Issuing business licenses to big food factories

explanation: As health workers, we put policy into action right at the clinic by checking children's growth and catching malnutrition early. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T18#GNS214_U1_T18_h6)

question: What is the main feature of Community-Based Health Insurance (CBHI) schemes?

options.A: They require patients to pay the full cost of surgery upfront
options.B: They are funded exclusively by international pharmaceutical companies
options.C: They are voluntary schemes where members pay regular local premiums
options.D: They are mandatory taxes collected by the federal government

explanation: CBHI relies on people within the community choosing to chip in regularly so they can share medical risks together. Simple and effective! [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h3)

question: What term is used when FGM is illegally performed inside a hospital or clinic by trained medical personnel?

options.A: Clinical harm reduction
options.B: Medicalization of FGM
options.C: Therapeutic intervention
options.D: Surgical modification

explanation: Spot on! 'Medicalization' means carrying out FGM in a health facility or by a health worker, which remains completely illegal and unethical. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T5#GNS225_U6_T5_h5)

question: What is a major risk when relying only on written charts during an audit?

options.A: Patients will refuse to take their prescribed hospital medications
options.B: Doctors will take over all the responsibilities of the nursing staff
options.C: Care might have been given but simply not documented by the nurse
options.D: Case notes might turn into digital files without any human input

explanation: Exactly! Heavy workloads on the ward sometimes mean a nurse performed a procedure wonderfully, but was simply too busy to write it down. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the main medical benefit of Female Genital Mutilation (FGM)?

options.A: It improves long-term reproductive health
options.B: It balances female reproductive hormones
options.C: It has no medical purpose or health benefits
options.D: It prevents common bacterial infections

explanation: You got this! FGM is done strictly for cultural or traditional reasons. It doesn't offer any health benefits to the body at all. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T1#GNS225_U6_T1_h1)

question: What is the main goal of nursing data integration?

options.A: Lowering the financial cost of hospital building maintenance
options.B: Replacing all human nurses with automated computer programs
options.C: Reducing the total number of hospital beds needed
options.D: Bringing patient information together into a single view

explanation: You've got this! Data integration simply means gathering scattered patient details from different places so you can see the whole picture in one spot. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h1)

question: What does Evidence-Based Practice primarily combine in clinical decision-making?

options.A: Research evidence, clinical expertise, and patient preferences
options.B: Pharmaceutical advertisements and medical textbook theory
options.C: Traditional habits, personal opinions, and trial-and-error
options.D: Hospital budget reports, doctor orders, and insurance rules

explanation: True evidence-based practice brings together solid research findings, the nurse's professional experience, and the values of the patient. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which fish should pregnant women avoid because of the risk of harming the baby's nervous system?

options.A: Low-fat white fish like tilapia and cod
options.B: Canned tuna in small weekly portions
options.C: Freshwater fish caught in local rivers
options.D: High-mercury fish like swordfish and shark

explanation: Fish like swordfish and shark carry higher mercury levels which can cross the placenta, so it's safest for mums to steer clear! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h5)

question: Why is smoking a cigarette near oxygen therapy a massive fire hazard?

options.A: Smokers are unable to handle oxygen equipment properly
options.B: Oxygen tanks release toxic gases when heated by smoke
options.C: Cigarettes automatically explode when they touch oxygen tubing
options.D: Oxygen feeds fires and makes flames spread with explosive speed

explanation: Medical oxygen makes fires burn super fast and extremely hot. Even a small spark near oxygen can turn into a dangerous blaze instantly. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T8#GNS324_U6_T8_h2)

question: What shape does a standard antibody molecule look like?

options.A: Y-shape
options.B: Ring shape
options.C: Flat sheet
options.D: Spiral helix

explanation: Antibodies are shaped like the letter 'Y'. The tips of the Y have variable sites that lock specifically onto matching foreign antigens. [learn more](GST114_U4_T1#GST114_U4_T1_h4)

question: What makes foetal hemoglobin different from adult hemoglobin?

options.A: It is produced exclusively in the placenta
options.B: It has a higher affinity for oxygen
options.C: It carries carbon dioxide instead of oxygen
options.D: It breaks down much faster in cold temperatures

explanation: Foetal hemoglobin grabs onto oxygen much more tightly, enabling the baby to extract oxygen from maternal blood. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h5)

question: Why must a nurse use a filter needle when drawing medication from a glass ampoule?

options.A: To make the plunger move more smoothly inside the barrel
options.B: To filter out bacteria present in the room air
options.C: To change the chemical pH of the liquid medicine
options.D: To prevent tiny glass shards from entering the syringe

explanation: Snapping the neck of a glass ampoule creates microscopic shards. A filter needle traps these fragments so they are not injected into the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h4)

question: What does a sudden, rapid change in a patient's weight usually point to in clinical practice?

options.A: Permanent alterations in height
options.B: Immediate changes in bone density
options.C: Fluctuations in body fluid balance
options.D: Rapid muscle tissue hypertrophy

explanation: When weight shifts overnight, it's almost always water gain or loss rather than actual tissue changes. Good thing to keep in mind on the ward! [learn more](GNS124_U6_T5#GNS124_U6_T5_h2)

question: What does family emotional health really mean?

options.A: A psychiatrist has officially declared the household stable
options.B: The family works together well and handles stress as a team
options.C: Everyone in the house is completely free from physical sickness
options.D: The family is rich and financially independent

explanation: Think of family emotional health as teamwork! It's about how the household communicates and supports each other through daily ups and downs, not just whether everyone is physically well. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why is hiding medical mistakes a bad idea in nursing?

options.A: It prevents nurses from charting properly
options.B: It increases the cost of hospital equipment
options.C: It always leads to immediate license revocation
options.D: It deepens trauma and damages patient trust

explanation: Hiding mistakes only makes things worse. It causes more emotional pain for families and completely destroys their trust in us as healthcare providers. [learn more](GST319_U6_T3#GST319_U6_T3_h1)

question: A patient develops sudden severe shortness of breath, restlessness, and absent breath sounds on the treated side after a thoracocentesis. What is the nurse's priority action?

options.A: Administer a mild oral pain medication and check vital signs in one hour
options.B: Remove the dressing and apply warm compresses to the puncture site
options.C: Encourage the patient to take slow, deep breaths to clear the airways
options.D: Notify the provider immediately and prepare for a chest tube insertion

explanation: Absent breath sounds and severe shortness of breath point to a significant pneumothorax or lung collapse, which is a medical emergency. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of health promotion?

options.A: Enabling people to increase control over and improve their health
options.B: Providing free medications to rural communities
options.C: Treating acute diseases in hospital settings
options.D: Isolating individuals with infectious conditions

explanation: Health promotion focuses on empowering individuals and communities to manage and better their overall well-being rather than just curing sickness. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h1)

question: A nurse wants to compare fall rates side by side for morning, afternoon, and night shifts across three different wards. Which chart type fits best?

options.A: Grouped bar chart
options.B: Pie chart
options.C: Simple bar chart
options.D: Histogram

explanation: A grouped bar chart allows multiple distinct bars per category, perfect for comparing shifts across multiple wards. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T7#GNS217_U4_T7_h3)

question: What does the clinical communication shortcut SBAR stand for?

options.A: Safety, Background, Analysis, Report
options.B: System, Barrier, Assessment, Recovery
options.C: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.D: Symptoms, Behavior, Action, Response

explanation: SBAR is your best friend during handovers and doctor calls! It keeps your communication clear, quick, and structured. [learn more](GST319_U5_T2#GST319_U5_T2_h7)

question: What is point prevalence?

options.A: Tracking the death rate from a single outbreak
options.B: Predicting how long a chronic illness will last
options.C: Calculating new infections over a five-year span
options.D: Measuring disease frequency at one specific moment

explanation: Point prevalence looks at a condition at a single, exact moment in time, like a photograph. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h2)

question: How can experiencing a severe illness during childhood affect a person later in life?

options.A: It ensures the individual becomes a proficient medical doctor
options.B: It completely eliminates any fear of normal aging processes
options.C: It can create a lasting hypersensitivity to bodily vulnerabilities
options.D: It guarantees immunity against developing anxiety disorders

explanation: Early life bumps and health scares can teach a child that the human body is super fragile, planting the seeds for health anxiety down the road. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h3)

question: A nurse is advising a low-risk traveler on where to stay during a 14-day observation period. Which option is most practical and commonly used?

options.A: Intensive care unit isolation room
options.B: Home quarantine with restricted movement
options.C: A high-security prison medical ward
options.D: The outpatient infectious disease clinic

explanation: For low-risk exposures without symptoms, home quarantine is the standard, practical approach to manage large numbers of people. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h3)

question: What does the term 'ex post facto' mean?

options.A: Before the intervention
options.B: Randomly assigned
options.C: During the experiment
options.D: After the fact

explanation: Easy peasy! 'Ex post facto' simply means 'after the fact'. The event has already happened, and we are looking backward to figure out what might have caused it. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T8#GNS224_U1_T8_h4)

question: A rural clinic lacks basic drugs and staff because government funds are delayed. What is the biggest immediate risk to patients?

options.A: Being overcharged by government health insurance schemes
options.B: Receiving free specialized surgeries at the local facility
options.C: Avoiding needed care or experiencing worsened health conditions
options.D: Enjoying excess medication supplies stored in the pharmacy

explanation: When clinics are empty and unfunded, sick people stay home, delay getting help, and unfortunately risk getting much worse. [learn more](GST322_U3_T3#GST322_U3_T3_h7)

question: A patient who previously appeared neat and well-groomed arrives at a follow-up visit looking disheveled with disorganized speech. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: A potential worsening of mental status or failing condition
options.B: That the physical assessment is completely unnecessary
options.C: That the patient has changed career paths successfully
options.D: Normal improvement in daily living skills

explanation: Negative changes in personal hygiene and disorganized speech often signal that a patient is relapsing or struggling. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a normal, healthy personality pattern?

options.A: Rigid and inflexible responses to everyday life stress
options.B: Ability to form deep and meaningful relationships with others
options.C: Realistic and honest perception of one's own self
options.D: Emotional flexibility when handling unexpected challenges

explanation: Rigid responses point toward a maladaptive pattern, whereas healthy personalities are flexible and adaptable. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T8#GNS314_U1_T8_h4)

question: What key role do community health nurses play when working with incoming NGO teams?

options.A: Managing financial audits for donor agencies
options.B: Funding the operational budgets of international organizations
options.C: Acting as a liaison to coordinate outreach schedules with local clinics
options.D: Drafting national health legislation in the federal assembly

explanation: Nurses are the vital bridge between visiting NGOs and local primary health centers, keeping patient care organized and steady. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T27#GNS225_U5_T27_h5)

question: What does 'personal liability' mean for you as a registered nurse?

options.A: Obligation to pay taxes on nursing salary directly to the medical board
options.B: Immunity from lawsuits if working inside a government facility
options.C: Accountability for one's own professional actions and nursing care
options.D: Financial responsibility for the entire hospital building and equipment

explanation: Personal liability means you are responsible for your own two hands. If you make a clinical error, you must answer for it individually. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h4)

question: Why should you avoid buying meat displayed openly without proper refrigeration in hot weather?

options.A: Unrefrigerated meat becomes too tough to chew
options.B: Heat and lack of cooling encourage rapid bacterial growth
options.C: Sunlight changes the protein structure into sugar
options.D: Meat exposed to air loses all of its iron content

explanation: Warm temperatures allow bacteria to multiply rapidly on raw meat, turning it into a hazard for foodborne illness. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h3)

question: How do standard daily contraceptive pills primarily prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By permanently blocking the fallopian tubes with scar tissue
options.B: By stopping ovulation and changing the cervical mucus
options.C: By killing all bacteria inside the vaginal canal
options.D: By neutralizing stomach acid so hormones cannot absorb

explanation: The hormones in the pill do a double-duty job: they tell the body to pause ovulation and make the cervical mucus thick so sperm can't get through. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the main danger of waiting for lab test results before treating certain severe poisonings?

options.A: Immediate kidney failure from drawing too much blood
options.B: Severe allergic reactions to the laboratory reagents
options.C: Automatic rejection of insurance claims by the hospital
options.D: Dangerous delays in giving life-saving therapy

explanation: In toxicology emergencies, clinical signs matter more than paperwork. Waiting on lab results can waste precious time while the poison takes over. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T7#GNS215_U5_T7_h4)

question: What is an endemic disease?

options.A: A rare disease that only appears once every century
options.B: A physical injury resulting from a motor vehicle accident
options.C: A medical condition caused entirely by eating too much sugar
options.D: An infection that is constantly present within a specific region

explanation: Endemic diseases, such as malaria in tropical climates, maintain a steady presence in the local area. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is the main difference between an 'output' and an 'outcome' in advocacy?

options.A: Outputs measure financial costs, while outcomes measure staff attendance
options.B: Outputs happen after the project, while outcomes happen before the project
options.C: Outputs measure activities done, while outcomes measure actual results achieved
options.D: Outputs are qualitative stories, while outcomes are strictly numerical charts

explanation: Think of outputs as what you *did* (like handing out 100 flyers), and outcomes as the actual *change* that happened because of it (like more people getting vaccinated). [learn more](GNS124_U4_T8#GNS124_U4_T8_h7)

question: A nurse accidentally pricks her finger with a hollow needle used to draw blood. What is the biggest worry?

options.A: Suffering from severe immediate muscle spasms
options.B: Developing an acute allergic reaction to latex
options.C: Developing localized skin necrosis on the finger
options.D: Exposure to bloodborne pathogens like HIV and Hepatitis

explanation: Hollow needles often hold infected blood inside them, which is why a prick poses a direct threat of viral transmission. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h3)

question: What is a major infrastructure challenge facing EHR implementation in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Unstable power supply and unreliable internet connectivity
options.B: Complete refusal of patients to allow digital data collection
options.C: Too many software options created by local nursing students
options.D: An overabundance of computer hardware in rural clinics

explanation: Consistent electricity and internet access are essential for digital health records, making power outages a major operational barrier. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h5)

question: Who is primarily responsible for providing Medical Nutrition Therapy (MNT)?

options.A: Registered Dietitians
options.B: Hospital security guards
options.C: Pharmaceutical sales reps
options.D: General ward nurses

explanation: Medical Nutrition Therapy requires specialized clinical training typically provided by registered dietitians. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h5)

question: What two things must be true for the rule of 'respondeat superior' to apply to a nurse's mistake?

options.A: An employer-employee relationship and action within the scope of employment
options.B: Written hospital policies and a signed malpractice insurance contract
options.C: A nursing license renewal and membership in a professional association
options.D: Direct supervision by a physician and a formal patient consent form

explanation: For the hospital to be pulled in, you must actually work there, and the mistake has to happen while you are doing your assigned job duties. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h2)

question: Which of the following conditions would NOT be considered a factor that impairs placental exchange efficiency?

options.A: Thickening of the placental membrane from infection
options.B: Maternal cigarette smoking
options.C: Increased maternal hydration and rest
options.D: Placental infarction

explanation: Normal rest and adequate hydration generally support good circulation, whereas infarctions, smoking, and infections actively damage placental exchange capacity. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h8)

question: Why is the real-world failure rate for natural methods usually higher than the textbook 'perfect use' rate?

options.A: Manufacturing defects occur in calendar charts
options.B: Human error and inconsistent tracking happen in daily life
options.C: Body temperature sensors expire after one month
options.D: Government policies restrict natural birth control methods

explanation: A method might look foolproof on paper, but real life gets busy! Missing a day of charting or miscalculating a window easily leads to human error. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T009#GNS226_U6_T009_h7)

question: How do nursing leaders use the information gathered from emergency debriefing sessions?

options.A: To permanently reduce the number of emergency personnel on shift
options.B: To replace all clinical staff with automated computer systems
options.C: To justify cutting funding for emergency equipment stockpiles
options.D: To update disaster protocols, refine triage checklists, and guide staff training

explanation: Lessons learned from past emergencies directly translate into better guidelines, improved tools, and sharper training for healthcare workers. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T1#GNS315_U5_T1_h7)

question: What three main disciplines are combined in nursing informatics?

options.A: Biology, pharmacology, and hospital administration
options.B: Nursing science, computer science, and information science
options.C: Public health, statistics, and clinical psychology
options.D: Medicine, engineering, and health economics

explanation: Nursing informatics is defined by the integration of nursing science with computer and information sciences to manage healthcare data. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which level of government is mainly responsible for funding general hospitals that provide secondary care?

options.A: Local government council
options.B: International donor agencies
options.C: Private voluntary organizations
options.D: State government

explanation: Great job! State ministries of health take charge of managing and funding general hospitals, which make up our secondary care tier. [learn more](GST322_U5_T4#GST322_U5_T4_h3)

question: A patient arrives with active pulmonary tuberculosis (TB). What kind of precautions should you set up right away?

options.A: Contact precautions
options.B: Droplet precautions
options.C: Airborne precautions
options.D: Standard precautions only

explanation: Correct! TB travels easily through tiny air particles, so you need airborne precautions like a special room and an N95 mask. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h3)

question: When working in homes and local clinics, what is a community nurse's most powerful tool for delivering care?

options.A: Prescription drug formularies
options.B: The nurse's own self and relational ability
options.C: Hospital electronic health record systems
options.D: Advanced diagnostic laboratory equipment

explanation: You don't always have fancy hospital gadgets in the community! Your ability to connect, talk, and build trust with people is your greatest tool. You've got this! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h1)

question: After gathering your data and setting priorities, what is the most important final output to create?

options.A: A practical action plan with goals, responsibilities, and timelines
options.B: An indefinite suspension of all community health outreaches
options.C: A private financial statement kept hidden from community leaders
options.D: A complex textbook filled with heavy medical Latin terms

explanation: Data is only helpful if we use it! Turning your findings into a clear, organized action plan guides your next steps as a nurse. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T8#GNS124_U3_T8_h6)

question: When is relying on an 'authority figure' most risky in clinical practice?

options.A: When the nurse is washing their hands before a procedure
options.B: When the textbook was published in the current year
options.C: When the hospital policy was written yesterday by a committee
options.D: When the authority figure speaks outside their specific field or is biased

explanation: Even brilliant experts can be wrong when talking about topics outside their actual specialty! [learn more](GNS217_U1_T3#GNS217_U1_T3_h3)

question: How do the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) differ from the earlier selective health approaches?

options.A: They rely only on private hospitals instead of community clinics
options.B: They focus exclusively on curing adult heart disease in wealthy nations
options.C: They completely ignore maternal and child health in favor of space research
options.D: They return to a broader, more comprehensive vision of health linked to overall development

explanation: SDG 3 and related goals embrace a wide-ranging view of health and well-being, echoing the holistic spirit of the original Alma-Ata declaration. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h5)

question: What do we call someone who carries and spreads a germ without looking or feeling sick?

options.A: A primary reservoir
options.B: An indirect vector
options.C: An asymptomatic carrier
options.D: A susceptible host

explanation: Correct! Asymptomatic carriers harbor and spread germs while feeling completely healthy themselves. That's why universal precautions matter so much! [learn more](GST114_U2_T1#GST114_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the main goal of preventive healthcare services in the community?

options.A: To cure advanced stages of chronic organ failure
options.B: To stop diseases from occurring in the first place
options.C: To manage emergency surgical trauma in hospitals
options.D: To replace the need for community health education

explanation: Preventive services aim to intercept disease processes before they start through immunizations, hygiene, and safe water practices. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h3)

question: What does a level one priority indicate on a standard emergency triage scale?

options.A: An infection requiring oral antibiotics only
options.B: Immediate life-threatening resuscitation needed
options.C: A stable patient ready for immediate discharge
options.D: A minor non-urgent medical complaint

explanation: Level one is reserved for critical emergencies like cardiac arrest or major trauma requiring instant life-saving actions. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T1#GNS315_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is usually the very first sign that makes a woman realize she needs to check her breast?

options.A: Severe, sharp pain throughout both breasts
options.B: Complete disappearance of the normal breast tissue
options.C: A hard, painless, and irregular breast lump
options.D: A sudden fever with generalized body weakness

explanation: A painless, hard lump is the classic red flag. Because it doesn't hurt at first, many women unfortunately ignore it. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h5)

question: What is the main job of bile when it comes to digesting fats?

options.A: Neutralizing stomach acid in the stomach lumen
options.B: Absorbing cholesterol directly into the bloodstream
options.C: Emulsifying large fat droplets into smaller pieces
options.D: Chemically breaking down fatty acids into simple sugars

explanation: Think of bile as natural dish soap for your food! It breaks big globs of fat into tiny droplets so digestive enzymes can easily mix in and finish the job. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T011#GNS227_U1_T011_h6)

question: What is the main job of agar in microbiology culture media?

options.A: To solidify liquid broth into a solid growth surface
options.B: To lower the temperature inside laboratory incubators
options.C: To provide extra oxygen for anaerobic bacteria
options.D: To stain bacterial cells under a light microscope

explanation: You nailed it! Agar comes from seaweed and acts like gelatin, turning liquid broth into a firm plate where colonies can grow nicely. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h4)

question: Why is keeping accurate, neat records so vital before you send off a referral?

options.A: It prevents the patient from visiting traditional birth attendants
options.B: It is required to qualify the clinic for international financial grants
options.C: It provides legal protection and proves what interventions were performed
options.D: It allows the nurse to charge extra consultation fees

explanation: You nailed it. Good notes protect you professionally by showing clear evidence of how you assessed, stabilized, and handed over the patient. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h5)

question: What is a great way to help busy clinic staff keep data accurate without burning them out?

options.A: Eliminate all documentation requirements permanently across all clinics
options.B: Increase the number of complex indicators they must track every hour
options.C: Punish staff publicly every time a single tally mark is out of place
options.D: Keep data collection tools simple and provide ongoing training on their value

explanation: When nurses understand *why* data matters and have simple tools to record it, reporting becomes much easier and accurate! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T21#GNS225_U2_T21_h7)

question: Why must dangerous infections like cholera be reported immediately to health authorities?

options.A: To ensure the hospital receives full financial reimbursement.
options.B: To update international travel visa records automatically.
options.C: To trigger rapid outbreak containment and protect the community.
options.D: To test new pharmaceutical drugs on infected populations.

explanation: Spot on! Quick reporting lets public health teams jump into action, find the source, and stop an epidemic before it spreads. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the main use of a daily vaccination tally sheet?

options.A: To track the monthly salary of the clinic staff
options.B: To record each vaccine dose given as it happens
options.C: To list the home addresses of unvaccinated adults
options.D: To calculate the expiry date of stored medicines

explanation: Tally sheets are handy paper or digital forms we use right in the clinic to tick off every single vaccine dose we administer daily. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T75#GNS214_U1_T75_h3)

question: What is the main job of a skilled birth attendant during a home delivery?

options.A: To transport the mother to a hospital for every contraction
options.B: To prescribe long-term contraception before labor starts
options.C: To perform emergency cesarean sections in the home
options.D: To monitor mother and baby and manage normal childbirth

explanation: You've got this! A skilled birth attendant is simply there to watch how labor progresses, support the mother, and safely handle a normal delivery while keeping an eye out for any trouble. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T7#GNS225_U3_T7_h1)

question: What is 'elite capture' in the context of community mobilisation?

options.A: When foreign donors pull out all financial support suddenly
options.B: When only wealthy or powerful individuals benefit from or control the project
options.C: When the local police arrest community health workers unjustly
options.D: When traditional healers refuse to speak with modern nurses

explanation: Elite capture happens when powerful community members take over resources meant for everyone. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h7)

question: Warfarin stops blood clotting by interfering with which substances in the liver?

options.A: Activated platelets
options.B: Antithrombin protein
options.C: Fibrinogen strands
options.D: Vitamin K dependent factors

explanation: Warfarin works right in the liver, blocking vitamin K so it can't help build those important clotting factors. You're learning fast! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h2)

question: What do we call a failure to use ordinary care that a reasonable nurse would show, resulting in patient harm?

options.A: Advocacy
options.B: Autonomy
options.C: Negligence
options.D: Battery

explanation: Correct! Negligence is basically careless nursing—failing to act with the standard of care expected, leading to accidental harm. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T5#GNS324_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which group represents formal health care providers in Nigeria?

options.A: Licensed nurses and doctors working in approved hospitals
options.B: Patent medicine vendors selling drugs without formal professional training
options.C: Unlicensed local bone setters practicing in rural markets
options.D: Traditional birth attendants operating in local communities

explanation: Awesome! Formal providers are officially trained, licensed, and regulated professionals like you are training to be! [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h5)

question: How do anticholinergic drugs help stop the airways from narrowing?

options.A: By blocking acetylcholine from attaching to muscarinic receptors
options.B: By replacing lost calcium ions in the muscle tissue
options.C: By destroying the enzymes that break down cAMP
options.D: By stimulating the sympathetic nervous system directly

explanation: Acetylcholine is a chemical that normally tells airways to squeeze shut. Anticholinergics block it from doing its job, keeping your airways nice and open. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T2#GNS223_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which part of the nervous system kicks in during a 'fight-or-flight' stress response?

options.A: Parasympathetic division
options.B: Central division
options.C: Sympathetic division
options.D: Somatic division

explanation: Spot on! The sympathetic system pumps up your heart rate and gets your body ready for action when you're stressed or scared. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the term for the process where the mother's body returns to its pre-pregnant state after delivery?

options.A: Duplication
options.B: Hypertrophy
options.C: Hemodilution
options.D: Involution

explanation: Involution refers to the rapid process by which the uterus and other body systems return to their non-pregnant size and condition. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h2)

question: What is the main reason doctors order a daily 'sedation vacation' for a ventilated patient?

options.A: To let the ventilator machine calibrate its internal sensors
options.B: To allow the nursing staff to take a scheduled meal break
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of medications in the unit
options.D: To evaluate the patient's neurological status and readiness for weaning

explanation: Pausing sedation for a short while lets us check how the patient's brain is doing and see if they are strong enough to start breathing on their own. Brilliant teamwork! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h6)

question: How does an infant acquire natural passive immunity from their mother?

options.A: Through receiving routine childhood routine immunizations
options.B: By producing antibodies after surviving a childhood illness
options.C: By inheriting active immune memory cells during conception
options.D: Through the transfer of maternal antibodies via breast milk

explanation: Maternal antibodies pass to the baby across the placenta and through breast milk, giving the newborn temporary protection against common infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h2)

question: Why is spreading unverified rumors during an emergency response so dangerous?

options.A: It increases the battery life of digital tracking dashboards
options.B: It automatically improves the physical infrastructure of the command center
options.C: It speeds up the distribution of medical supplies to remote areas
options.D: It can cause public panic and lead to the misallocation of ambulances and resources

explanation: False rumors cause chaos, often sending critical ambulances and rescue teams to places that don't actually need them. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T1#GNS315_U5_T1_h5)

question: When is it legally okay for a nurse to share a patient's private medical diagnosis with someone else?

options.A: When a curious neighbor asks about the patient's illness.
options.B: When the nurse wants to discuss interesting cases on social media.
options.C: When the hospital manager asks casually out of curiosity.
options.D: When required by statute or public health laws for specific diseases.

explanation: Patient confidentiality is sacred, but the law allows exceptions when reporting public health threats (like certain infectious diseases or gunshot wounds) to the appropriate authorities. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h7)

question: Why is it risky to rely solely on blood albumin levels to assess a sick patient's nutrition?

options.A: Albumin changes too slowly to be useful in a hospital setting.
options.B: Inflammation and fluid changes can alter albumin levels regardless of diet.
options.C: Blood tests for albumin are completely unreliable in all humans.
options.D: Albumin only measures how much water is inside the stomach.

explanation: Albumin is an acute-phase reactant; inflammation and fluid overload can lower its level even if the patient is well-nourished. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h6)

question: How do clinical software apps differ from system software?

options.A: Clinical apps perform specific job tasks like charting, while system software manages the computer itself.
options.B: System software is designed for patients, while clinical apps are for doctors only.
options.C: Clinical apps can only run without an operating system present.
options.D: Clinical apps are physical hardware parts, while system software is purely digital.

explanation: Clinical apps help you do your actual job (like charting vitals), while system software keeps the machine running behind the scenes. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why did early healers perform trephining (drilling a hole in the skull) on people with mental illness?

options.A: To relieve increased pressure from a stroke
options.B: To allow trapped evil spirits to escape
options.C: To cure long-standing chronic migraines
options.D: To treat severe bacterial brain infections

explanation: It sounds wild today! They literally cut a hole in the skull because they thought it would let the bad spirits out of the person's head. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which type of injury happens primarily from breathing in superheated air and smoke?

options.A: Surgical disruption
options.B: Inhalational injury
options.C: Blunt neck trauma
options.D: Penetrating trauma

explanation: Well done! Heat and toxic chemicals from smoke directly burn and damage the delicate lining of the upper airway. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T5#GNS213_U2_T5_h2)

question: A resident says they already took their morning blood pressure pill, but the medication administration record (MAR) is blank for that time. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Administer a second dose immediately to ensure their blood pressure stays controlled
options.B: Wait until the evening shift to see if the blood pressure spikes
options.C: Assume the resident is correct and sign the record as given by the resident
options.D: Withhold the dose and consult the prescribing physician or charge nurse before acting

explanation: Brilliant! Giving a double dose can be dangerous. Always pause, check the facts, and consult your senior colleagues or doctor when something doesn't match up. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h5)

question: What is a main reason fresh fruits spoil so fast after harvest in hot climates?

options.A: Excessive consumption of vegetables by local farmers
options.B: Inadequate cold storage and refrigeration facilities
options.C: Overly strict international export quality standards
options.D: The use of organic seeds instead of commercial hybrids

explanation: Correct! Without good refrigeration in hot weather, fresh produce unfortunately goes bad before it ever gets to market. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T030#GNS227_U2_T030_h7)

question: What was the first major antipsychotic medication discovered in the 1950s?

options.A: Lithium carbonate
options.B: Diazepam
options.C: Chlorpromazine
options.D: Fluoxetine

explanation: Chlorpromazine was the pioneering antipsychotic drug that revolutionized the medical management of severe psychiatric disorders. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h5)

question: What factor can significantly alter a child's vital sign readings during a home assessment?

options.A: The time of the family meal
options.B: The brand of soap used at home
options.C: Crying or anxiety
options.D: The color of the bedroom wall

explanation: Correct! Fear, anxiety, or crying can cause a child's heart rate and breathing to jump up temporarily. Always keep that in mind during assessments! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h3)

question: When should rehabilitation nursing care ideally begin for a patient with a neurological issue?

options.A: Only after the patient is discharged to a nursing home
options.B: Several months after all acute symptoms have faded away
options.C: As soon as the patient is medically stable, often on day one
options.D: Once the patient asks to start physical therapy exercises

explanation: Early rehab stops stiff joints and contractures before they start, giving the brain the best possible head start on recovery. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T23#GNS222_U3_T23_h8)

question: Why did Florence Nightingale use visual diagrams like her famous polar area chart?

options.A: To hide negative hospital statistics from military generals
options.B: To predict future disease outbreaks in European cities
options.C: To make complex data easy for non-medical leaders to understand
options.D: To decorate official reports for the royal family

explanation: Visual charts helped politicians and military commanders quickly grasp the shocking death toll caused by poor hygiene rather than battle wounds. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why do nurses often treat life threats at the exact same time they assess the patient in an emergency?

options.A: Because hospital regulations require double documentation for all tasks
options.B: Because doctors prefer to delegate all physical tasks to students
options.C: Because waiting to treat life threats while finishing an assessment can be fatal
options.D: Because nurses have too much free time during shifts

explanation: In critical care, assessment and treatment happen together. A dying patient cannot wait for a slow, complete exam! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T2#GNS315_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why does a repeat infection with the same virus trigger a much faster immune response?

options.A: Memory B-cells formed during the first infection quickly recognize the virus.
options.B: Red blood cells absorb the viral toxins before they reach the lymph nodes.
options.C: Innate white blood cells stop destroying friendly bacteria in the gut.
options.D: The body's skin barriers become thicker to prevent the virus from entering.

explanation: Memory B-cells remember past battles, letting your body skip the slow setup phase and fight back instantly. [learn more](GST114_U4_T5#GST114_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why does long-term poverty often contribute to higher rates of mental health issues?

options.A: Financial worries completely eliminate the need for sleep
options.B: Wealthy people are immune to all forms of emotional distress
options.C: Poor people choose to have weaker brain chemistry
options.D: It exposes individuals to continuous, inescapable daily stress and insecurity

explanation: When someone is constantly struggling to survive and pay bills day after day, their brain's coping reserves get completely worn down. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T1#GNS314_U4_T1_h5)

question: What does the term Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) actually measure?

options.A: The percentage of water reabsorbed in the loop of Henle
options.B: The speed at which blood travels through the renal artery
options.C: The total amount of urine excreted per day
options.D: The volume of fluid filtered by the kidneys per minute

explanation: GFR quantifies how much filtrate the kidneys produce across all glomeruli in a given minute, serving as a key indicator of kidney health. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h5)

question: Which body regulates the professional scope of practice for midwives in Nigeria?

options.A: West African Health Organization
options.B: Nigerian Medical Association
options.C: Federal Ministry of Women Affairs
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria is the statutory body responsible for setting standards and regulating midwifery practice. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of bilateral tubal ligation?

options.A: Permanent female contraception
options.B: Treatment for severe pelvic infections
options.C: Prevention of ovarian hormone production
options.D: Regulation of irregular menstrual cycles

explanation: Tubal ligation is specifically designed as a permanent surgical method to prevent pregnancy by blocking the fallopian tubes. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h1)

question: Which teaching principle means we should start with what matters most to the patient right now?

options.A: Repetition
options.B: Active participation
options.C: Relevance
options.D: Strict discipline

explanation: You got it! When we talk about things that touch their daily lives and immediate worries, patients listen and learn much faster. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h2)

question: Which of the following is classified as pathological waste?

options.A: Used paper hand towels
options.B: Broken mercury thermometers
options.C: Surgically removed human tissues
options.D: Expired paracetamol tablets

explanation: Pathological waste specifically includes human tissues, organs, and body parts removed during surgeries or autopsies. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h2)

question: What term describes the fatty, foul-smelling stools seen in patients with chronic pancreatitis?

options.A: Steatorrhea
options.B: Acholuria
options.C: Hematochezia
options.D: Melena

explanation: Great recall! Steatorrhea is the medical term for fatty, oily stools. It happens because the damaged pancreas can't make the enzymes needed to digest fats properly. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h4)

question: A critically ill patient on oxygen support needs to be transferred to the CT scan room. Who is best suited to accompany this patient?

options.A: A qualified nurse or doctor with portable oxygen and emergency gear
options.B: An administrative clerk who knows the shortcut hallways well
options.C: The patient's visiting relative who agreed to watch the monitor
options.D: A hospital security guard who can help push the wheeled trolley

explanation: Unstable or critically ill patients must always be escorted by trained clinical staff equipped to handle sudden emergencies during transit. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h5)

question: A patient scheduled for parole review keeps refusing meds and denies being sick. What should the team do first?

options.A: Approve the release immediately to encourage independence.
options.B: Delay the release until their insight and compliance improve.
options.C: Ignore the medication refusal since it is a minor issue.
options.D: Discharge the patient with no follow-up requirements.

explanation: Safety first! Refusing medication and lacking insight are big warning signs that a patient isn't quite ready for independent community living yet. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T8#GNS314_U5_T8_h2)

question: What is the main goal of inferential statistics in nursing research?

options.A: To draw pictures and graphs of patient medical records
options.B: To make guesses about a large group based on a small study group
options.C: To calculate the exact average age of patients in a single ward
options.D: To store patient health history in a computer database

explanation: Spot on! Since we can't study every single patient in Nigeria, we use a smaller group (sample) to draw conclusions about the wider population. You've got this! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T3#GNS217_U4_T3_h1)

question: What does the 'C' stand for in the ABCDE pre-hospital emergency care framework?

options.A: Consciousness
options.B: Cardiac
options.C: Collapse
options.D: Circulation

explanation: In emergency trauma care, C stands for Circulation, focusing on checking pulses and stopping severe bleeding. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T3#GNS315_U5_T3_h6)

question: Why is drinking enough water important for protecting a susceptible host?

options.A: It directly destroys bacterial cell walls in the bloodstream
options.B: It replaces the need for standard vaccinations
options.C: It permanently eliminates all body toxins
options.D: It keeps mucosal membranes moist to trap foreign particles

question: Why is psychological rehab just as vital as physical detox when treating substance dependence?

question: Why do health programs often fail when they are imposed from the outside without community involvement?

explanation: At the end of the day, everything we do in nursing research is about finding better ways to help our patients heal safely at the bedside. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is a very common emotional challenge for people dealing with untreated hearing loss?

options.A: Improved cognitive processing
options.B: Heightened sense of euphoria
options.C: Increased physical strength
options.D: Social isolation and depression

question: Why is waste segregation at the point of generation considered so important in healthcare facilities?

options.A: It reduces the physical weight of general rubbish bins
options.B: It allows the hospital to recycle all medical waste into children's toys
options.C: It ensures hazardous infectious waste is treated correctly before final disposal
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for cleaning hospital floors

explanation: Separating waste immediately prevents infectious materials from mixing with ordinary household rubbish, protecting everyone from accidental contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h8)

question: Which prenatal event is most associated with an increased risk of neurological learning differences?

options.A: Severe oxygen deprivation during delivery
options.B: Taking prescribed prenatal vitamins daily
options.C: Mild morning sickness during the first trimester
options.D: A pregnant mother eating a high-protein diet

explanation: Perinatal complications like oxygen shortage can disrupt normal brain development, leading to later learning difficulties. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h3)

question: How has occupational health nursing changed from the 19th century to the 21st century?

options.A: From working exclusively in hospital wards to running corporate legal departments
options.B: From addressing traumatic physical injuries in heavy factories to managing chronic strain and mental wellness
options.C: From ignoring chemical exposures entirely to treating only rare tropical diseases
options.D: From focusing exclusively on boardroom management to supervising mining operations

explanation: While physical safety is still key, today's occupational nurses focus a lot on ergonomics, mental health, and preventing everyday work stress. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T1#GNS225_U7_T1_h6)

question: Which sign strongly points to a uterine infection instead of normal side effects?

options.A: Nausea that goes away in a day
options.B: Chills lasting only for the first two hours
options.C: Foul-smelling vaginal discharge and persistent fever
options.D: Cramping that feels worse than a normal period
