question: What is the tiny, functional building block of compact bone called?

options.A: Osteon
options.B: Trabecula
options.C: Periosteum
options.D: Epiphysis

explanation: An osteon is just the neat, cylinder-shaped repeating unit that makes up hard compact bone. Brilliant work! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T4#GNS121_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the best immediate action to control heavy bleeding from a wound on someone's arm?

options.A: Giving the patient large amounts of oral fluids
options.B: Elevating the arm above the level of the heart only
options.C: Applying direct pressure with a clean dressing
options.D: Pouring rubbing alcohol directly into the open cut

explanation: Awesome! Direct pressure is your best friend here. It squeezes the bleeding vessels against the bone so a clot can quickly form. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why do nurses need to watch a patient closely after they get IV contrast dye for a scan?

options.A: To watch for delayed allergic reactions and kidney stress
options.B: To measure how fast the dye exits through sweat glands
options.C: To prevent the intravenous site from leaking sterile water
options.D: To ensure the patient does not fall asleep too quickly

explanation: Contrast dye can sometimes trigger sneaky allergic reactions or put extra stress on the kidneys, so post-procedure monitoring is a must. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h8)

question: What is a practical way an educator can check the physical learning environment?

options.A: Require students to buy their own classroom air conditioners
options.B: Regularly monitor classroom comfort levels like temperature and lighting
options.C: Hold all lectures outdoors regardless of weather conditions
options.D: Lock the classroom doors to eliminate outside hallway noise

explanation: Good teachers pay attention to their surroundings, making sure the room is comfortable enough for students to focus and absorb clinical concepts. [learn more](GST321_U8_T9#GST321_U8_T9_h6)

question: What does reproductive health truly mean according to the World Health Organization (WHO)?

options.A: A woman's physical capability to carry a pregnancy to full term safely
options.B: The total absence of any bacteria or viruses in the pelvic organs
options.C: The biological ability to conceive and bear children without medical help
options.D: A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being in all reproductive matters

explanation: Think of reproductive health as more than just working body parts. The WHO looks at the whole person—physical, mental, and social well-being together! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h1)

question: What does the First-In, First-Out (FIFO) storage rule mean?

options.A: Using older food items before newer ones
options.B: Throwing away food on the first day of purchase
options.C: Cooking all food items on the same day
options.D: Placing new food items at the front of the shelf

explanation: FIFO ensures older stock is used first so nothing sits long enough to spoil or pass its expiration date. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h8)

question: Why is the brain stem such an important connection point in the nervous system?

options.A: It connects the higher brain centers to the spinal cord.
options.B: It produces all the cerebrospinal fluid for the brain.
options.C: It controls conscious thought and creative reasoning.
options.D: It stores long-term memories for the cerebral cortex.

explanation: The main job of the brain stem is to act as a busy highway, linking the brain above directly to the spinal cord below. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h1)

question: Why does widespread use of antibiotics naturally lead to more resistant germs?

options.A: Drugs cause healthy human cells to mutate into resistant bacteria
options.B: Pathogens learn to consume the antibiotic drugs as a primary food source
options.C: Medicines expire quickly in tropical climates and lose their potency
options.D: Surviving microbes pass on their protective traits to the next generation

explanation: Think of it like survival of the fittest. When weak germs are killed off, the tough ones left behind breed and pass on their protective superpowers to their offspring! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T92#GNS214_U1_T92_h1)

question: What is a major focus of nursing research in settings like Nigeria today?

options.A: Designing private space rockets for healthcare workers
options.B: Reducing maternal mortality and improving community health
options.C: Testing luxury spa treatments for hospital patients
options.D: Replacing all clinical nurses with computer robots

explanation: Spot on! Local nursing research here at home focuses on solving pressing local issues, especially keeping mothers and children healthy in our communities. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT an ethical requirement during a health screening exercise?

options.A: Keeping client test results strictly confidential
options.B: Respecting the cultural beliefs of the client
options.C: Forcing clients to participate even if they refuse
options.D: Explaining the limitations of the screening test

explanation: Correct! Screening must always be voluntary. Forcing a client goes completely against patient rights and nursing ethics. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T5#GNS123_U2_T5_h6)

question: What does a 'just culture' in nursing try to balance?

options.A: Accountability for choices with understanding of system flaws
options.B: Zero documentation with total reliance on verbal handovers
options.C: Strict punishment for every single near miss that occurs
options.D: Financial profit margins with patient satisfaction scores

explanation: A just culture is fair: it holds people responsible for reckless choices, but supports them when honest human errors or system flaws happen. [learn more](GST319_U5_T5#GST319_U5_T5_h8)

question: What is the main focus of 'validity' when creating a research tool?

options.A: Whether the tool gives the exact same score every single time
options.B: How many patients can complete the form in ten minutes
options.C: How cheap the research instrument is to buy in bulk
options.D: Whether the tool measures what it is supposed to measure

explanation: Validity is about hitting the bullseye! If you want to measure patient anxiety, a valid tool actually captures anxiety, not physical pain or hunger. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T27#GNS224_U1_T27_h2)

question: How does Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) help prevent HIV?

options.A: It is given as a one-time vaccine to provide lifelong immunity.
options.B: It is taken only after a person knows they have been exposed to the virus.
options.C: It kills existing opportunistic infections in AIDS patients.
options.D: It is taken daily by HIV-negative people to block the virus from establishing an infection.

explanation: Think of PrEP as a daily shield. People who are HIV-negative take it regularly to keep the virus from setting up shop if exposure happens. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T4#GNS214_U1_T4_h4)

question: When should a nurse researcher use the median instead of the mean?

options.A: When the data contains extreme outliers or is heavily skewed
options.B: When every single data point needs to be included in the calculation
options.C: When working exclusively with large, perfectly symmetrical bell curves
options.D: When the data represents simple categorical groups with no numbers

explanation: The median ignores extreme highs and lows, giving you a much truer picture of the center when your data is lopsided. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T4#GNS217_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which of these is a common cultural barrier to good nutrition for some Nigerian teenage girls?

options.A: A total lack of local markets selling staple foods
options.B: Cultural food taboos that save protein-rich foods for adult males
options.C: Mandatory government laws banning green vegetables
options.D: Traditional ceremonies forcing teens to fast for whole months

explanation: True! Some traditional practices mistakenly keep young girls from eating nourishing foods like eggs, meat, or fish. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T010#GNS227_U2_T010_h6)

question: Which type of white blood cell is mainly responsible for the humoral immune response?

options.A: B cells
options.B: Red blood cells
options.C: Platelets
options.D: T cells

explanation: B cells run the humoral response! They mature into plasma cells that pump out helpful antibodies into your body fluids. [learn more](GST114_U4_T1#GST114_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is the protective protein coat that surrounds the genetic material of a virus called?

options.A: Flagellum
options.B: Cellulose wall
options.C: Capsid
options.D: Peptidoglycan

explanation: The capsid acts like a tough little armor shell protecting the virus's genetic code from the outside world. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is a major plus of using comfort measures (like heat or rest) alongside medicines?

options.A: They guarantee the patient will have zero bleeding
options.B: They help reduce the overall need for heavy pain medications
options.C: They completely eliminate the need for any vital sign checks
options.D: They cure underlying infections without antibiotics

explanation: Combining simple comfort tricks with meds gives wonderful relief while keeping heavy drug use to a minimum. You're thinking like a holistic nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h4)

question: What is a helpful early nursing action for a survivor who is panicking right after a disaster?

options.A: Leaving the patient entirely alone in a dark room until they calm down
options.B: Telling them to stop crying because others have worse injuries
options.C: Offering calming reassurance, active listening, and simple factual information
options.D: Administering high-dose antipsychotic medications immediately

explanation: Well done! Psychological first aid is all about being present, listening calmly, and speaking gently to help bring someone back to a sense of safety. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T2#GNS315_U1_T2_h7)

question: A nurse is caring for four emergency patients. Which patient should the nurse attend to FIRST?

options.A: A patient with a minor scalp laceration needing stitches
options.B: A patient with a closed wrist fracture in mild pain
options.C: A patient with severe stridor and throat swelling
options.D: A patient complaining of a mild headache for three days

explanation: Stridor indicates an upper airway obstruction, which is an immediate life threat that takes top priority over pain or minor injuries. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h8)

question: Which of the following is a classic example of an obstetric emergency?

options.A: Severe postpartum hemorrhage
options.B: Chronic knee osteoarthritis
options.C: A mild seasonal allergy
options.D: Routine pregnancy checkup

explanation: Heavy bleeding after childbirth is a life-threatening emergency unique to obstetric care. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T1#GNS315_U2_T1_h4)

question: A patient with severe arthritis in one knee gets a direct steroid injection into the joint. What is the main benefit?

options.A: It lets the drug bypass the liver to enter the brain instantly.
options.B: It gives high drug concentration at the problem site while sparing the rest of the body.
options.C: It completely cures the underlying autoimmune disease.
options.D: It guarantees no side effects like high blood pressure.

explanation: Correct! Giving the injection right into the knee treats the local pain while keeping whole-body side effects as low as possible. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h3)

question: Why is recording an accurate pregnancy history so important for an expectant mother?

options.A: It guarantees that she will not experience any surgical complications.
options.B: It proves whether her previous babies were born with birth defects.
options.C: It identifies if her past pregnancies put her at a higher medical risk now.
options.D: It determines the exact date of conception for the current pregnancy.

explanation: Knowing the exact number of past viable births helps the healthcare team prepare for potential issues tied to many previous pregnancies, such as bleeding or placental problems. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T008#GNS226_U4_T008_h1)

question: Which strategy helps address community resistance toward half-way houses?

options.A: Public health education and community sensitization
options.B: Building high electric fences with armed military guards
options.C: Hiding the location of the house from everyone secretly
options.D: Refusing to let residents ever step outside the gate

explanation: Spot on! Educating the public helps clear up myths about mental illness and encourages local communities to welcome recovering individuals with open arms. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h7)

question: What is the job of pepsinogen once it is inside the stomach?

options.A: It converts into active pepsin to break down proteins
options.B: It lines the stomach wall to protect it from ulcers
options.C: It stimulates the release of bile from the liver
options.D: It neutralizes excess stomach acid

explanation: Chief cells release pepsinogen as a safe, inactive form. Once stomach acid hits it, it turns into active pepsin to start chopping up proteins! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h4)

question: A patient arrives at a triage post walking, talking, and only has minor scrapes and a broken wrist. What triage tag do they get?

options.A: Black tag
options.B: Red tag
options.C: Green tag
options.D: Yellow tag

question: Why must reusable equipment like stethoscopes be wiped with disinfectant between patients?

options.A: To prevent cross-contamination and hospital-acquired infections
options.B: To keep the metal parts from rusting in humid weather
options.C: To remove any manufacturer dust from the surface
options.D: To ensure the sound quality remains clear for hearing

question: Why do nurses need to know about parasitic ova?

options.C: To synthesize new anti-parasitic medications in the lab
options.D: To help confirm parasite infections through lab results

question: A hospital wants to check if their new nurse-led clinic actually lowered stroke rates over the past 5 years. What type of activity is this?

options.A: Evaluation, because it looks at long-term outcomes and overall impact
options.B: Monitoring, because it tracks daily blood pressure checks
options.C: Budgeting, because it calculates the cost of stethoscopes
options.D: Auditing, because it checks if nurses sign patient charts

explanation: Looking back over several years to see if health truly improved is a big-picture evaluation, not just daily monitoring. [learn more](GST319_U4_T5#GST319_U4_T5_h2)

question: Which historic international conference officially launched the modern concept of Primary Health Care (PHC) back in 1978?

options.A: The Abuja Health Summit

question: What is a major negative effect of HIV-related stigma in our communities?

options.A: It eliminates the need for VCT clinics.

options.C: It increases the effectiveness of antiretroviral drugs.
options.D: It causes the HIV virus to mutate into a weaker strain.

explanation: Fear of being judged makes people hide their status and stay away from clinics. Compassion and education are our best tools to fight this stigma! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T4#GNS214_U1_T4_h9)

question: A gifted child gets extremely upset over loud noises or small unfairness in class. What explains this?

options.A: Oppositional defiant tendencies
options.B: Sensory and emotional overexcitabilities
options.C: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
options.D: Typical delayed impulse control

question: How do the intrinsic and extrinsic pathways work together in the body?

options.A: They both activate a series of clotting factors that lead into the common pathway
options.B: They regulate the exact volume of blood pumped by the heart
options.C: They prevent platelets from sticking to healthy blood vessels
options.D: They work in opposite directions to dissolve unwanted blood clots

explanation: Both pathways act as separate starting points that eventually feed into the same shared sequence to produce a solid clot. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h3)

question: Your patient looks drowsy, confused, and is working hard just to breathe using their neck muscles. What is your best next step?

options.A: Apply a standard nasal cannula with low flow
options.B: Prepare for immediate respiratory support
options.C: Encourage the patient to sleep it off
options.D: Wait for laboratory blood test results

explanation: When a patient is this exhausted and using accessory muscles, they are tiring out fast. Getting respiratory support ready right away can save their life! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T5#GNS315_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which family planning method protects against both pregnancy AND sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

options.A: Hormonal implants
options.B: Copper intrauterine devices
options.C: Barrier methods
options.D: Natural fertility awareness

explanation: Great job! Barrier methods like male and female condoms block physical contact and fluids, giving you dual protection against both STIs and unwanted pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T008#GNS226_U6_T008_h2)

question: A nurse walks into a ward and finds a junior colleague throwing a used syringe into a regular black polythene bag. What is the most appropriate action?

options.A: Correct the colleague immediately and ensure the syringe is moved to the sharps box
options.B: Ignore the mistake because cleaners will sort it out later anyway
options.C: Write an official query letter to the hospital medical director
options.D: Remove all waste bins from the ward to teach everyone a lesson

explanation: Nurses have a duty to correct segregation errors instantly to maintain a safe working and clinical environment. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h7)

question: A patient on a hot day has been standing for hours at a parade and suddenly feels weak and collapses. What is the most likely trigger?

options.A: Peripheral blood pooling from heat and standing
options.B: A sudden increase in intracranial brain pressure
options.C: An acute blockage in the coronary arteries
options.D: An unrecognized epileptic seizure disorder

question: Which task is primarily the responsibility of the registered nurse in home health care?

options.A: Performing comprehensive initial clinical assessments
options.B: Preparing daily meals for the recovering patient
options.C: Prescribing new medications for chronic diseases
options.D: Installing wheelchair ramps and home safety rails

explanation: Registered nurses evaluate the patient's overall health status upon admission and coordinate the initial nursing care plan. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major social determinant of health in Nigeria?

options.A: Availability of clean water and rural infrastructure
options.B: The brand of stethoscope used by attending physicians
options.C: Maternal education and literacy rates
options.D: Household income and overall poverty levels

explanation: Medical equipment brand does not determine public health outcomes, whereas income, education, and water supply profoundly affect community well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why do we need different sectors (like health, police, and fire) to work together during a major disaster?

options.A: Different agencies bring specialized skills, equipment, and resources that one group lacks
options.B: It prevents local volunteers from taking credit for successful rescues
options.C: It ensures that only the military makes medical decisions for victims
options.D: It eliminates the need for any pre-planning or emergency simulation drills

explanation: No single agency can do it all! Combining medical, security, and rescue teams ensures everyone gets the complete care they need. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h5)

question: Which of these best describes the labia minora?

options.B: They are thick pads of fatty tissue
options.C: They produce mature ova
options.D: They cover the pubic symphysis

question: What is the main goal of sterilization in a clinic?

options.A: To reduce the number of bacteria to a safe, acceptable level
options.B: To remove visible dirt and grease from surgical instruments
options.C: To completely destroy all forms of microbial life and spores
options.D: To kill only active bacteria while leaving spores intact

explanation: Sterilization is our highest level of germ control! It wipes out every single microbe, including tough spores that love to hide. You've got this! [learn more](GST114_U2_T11#GST114_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why are heart muscle cells branched instead of straight?

options.A: To connect with multiple neighboring cells and form a synchronized network
options.B: To allow the heart to store extra glycogen reserves
options.C: To increase the speed of nerve impulse transmission from the brain
options.D: To prevent the heart muscle from undergoing aerobic respiration

explanation: Think of it like a handshake network! Branching helps every single cell link up with its neighbors so the whole heart can beat smoothly and together. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T10#GNS121_U3_T10_h1)

question: What major change did the Nursing Home Reform Act of 1987 introduce regarding resident management?

options.A: It removed all requirements for regular state health inspections
options.B: It placed severe restrictions on the use of physical and chemical restraints
options.C: It encouraged facilities to lock residents in rooms for safety
options.D: It mandated that all residents must take daily sedative medications

explanation: The 1987 law stepped in because restraints were often used just to make life easier for staff rather than keeping patients safe. The law heavily cracked down on this practice! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T5#GNS324_U5_T5_h4)

question: As a nurse, which quick bedside check helps detect nervous system irritability in a pregnant patient?

options.A: Listening for bowel sounds in all four quadrants
options.B: Testing the sense of taste and smell
options.C: Checking deep tendon reflexes
options.D: Measuring the circumference of the skull

explanation: Checking reflexes is a quick, non-invasive way to spot nervous system irritation, especially when monitoring for preeclampsia. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T6#GNS121_U7_T6_h6)

question: Which type of computer is designed to handle continuous physical measurements, like tracking pressure waves?

options.A: Digital computer
options.B: Hybrid computer
options.C: Microcomputer
options.D: Analog computer

explanation: Great try! Analog computers deal with smooth, continuous physical changes (like a wave or voltage) rather than counting separate numbers like 1, 2, 3. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the main goal of medical asepsis?

options.A: To eliminate every single microbial spore in the room
options.B: To sterilize surgical instruments before an operation
options.C: To reduce the number of pathogens and prevent their spread
options.D: To treat active bacterial infections with strong antibiotics

explanation: Medical asepsis focuses on keeping germ numbers low using clean techniques like handwashing to stop disease spread. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h3)

question: In Dorothea Orem's theory, what exactly does a 'self-care deficit' mean?

options.A: The hospital has run out of supplies needed for patient hygiene
options.B: The doctor has forbidden the patient from eating solid foods
options.C: The patient's need for self-care is greater than their ability to do it
options.D: The nurse refuses to help the patient walk around the ward

explanation: You nailed it. A self-care deficit simply happens when the care a person needs is higher than what they are currently able to pull off by themselves. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why should nurses pay close attention to a patient's emotional well-being while they are physically sick?

options.A: Patients with good emotions never require surgical interventions
options.B: Hospital policies mandate psychiatric evaluations for everyone
options.C: It replaces the need for administering prescribed medications
options.D: Emotional balance directly influences physical healing and recovery times

explanation: The mind and body are tightly linked. When a patient is emotionally overwhelmed or stressed, it can actually slow down their physical healing and immune system. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T5#GNS314_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why does getting pregnant at an older maternal age carry a higher risk of chromosomal issues in the baby?

options.A: The uterus loses its ability to protect the developing fetus over time
options.B: Sperm cells from older partners damage the egg's chromosomes
options.C: Primary oocytes stay arrested for decades, increasing the risk of errors during cell division
options.D: Hormone levels drop so low that follicles stop growing altogether

explanation: Remember that a woman's eggs stay paused in her ovaries for decades! Over time, the cellular machinery can get a bit tired, making errors slightly more likely during cell division. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T9#GNS121_U5_T9_h7)

question: Why must a hospital's internal policy always respect national nursing council regulations?

options.A: National councils pay for the printing of hospital rulebooks
options.B: It makes the hospital paperwork look neat and organized
options.C: Lower-level policies can never contradict higher regulatory frameworks
options.D: It allows nurses to ignore doctors' written prescriptions

explanation: In healthcare law, local rules must always align with and support higher national laws and professional board regulations. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h3)

question: A nurse manager refuses to share a patient's secret diagnosis, believing that keeping confidentiality is a universal moral rule no matter what. Which theory is this?

options.A: Utilitarianism
options.B: Systems theory
options.C: Scientific management
options.D: Deontology

explanation: Deontology is all about strict moral duties and rules ("doing the right thing because it's your duty"), no matter what the outcome might be. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h3)

question: A nurse is getting ready for surgery and notices a fresh scratch on the back of her hand. What should she do?

options.A: Rub antiseptic over it and wear double gloves
options.B: Report the scratch and take on a non-sterile role
options.C: Scrub for a longer time using special soap
options.D: Cover it tightly with a waterproof plaster and go ahead

explanation: Safety first! Open cuts let bacteria escape into the sterile field, so it's best to step back and take a non-sterile duty. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h2)

question: A community has strong local leadership and plenty of food supplies even though droughts happen often. What do we call these strengths?

options.A: A structural mitigation measure
options.B: An indicator of high vulnerability
options.C: A primary environmental hazard
options.D: A community capacity resource

explanation: Well done! Capacities are simply the strengths and resources a community uses to stand strong against disasters. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h2)

question: What document is the main source when a nurse compiles monthly health summaries?

options.A: Daily facility registers and tally sheets
options.B: Personal diary notes written by individual patients
options.C: The national constitution and health laws
options.D: Annual financial audit reports from local banks

explanation: Your monthly report is just the grand total of all those daily tallies and registers you filled out throughout the month. Keep them neat! [learn more](GNS124_U6_T2#GNS124_U6_T2_h6)

question: Why is depending only on human brainpower and focus a risky strategy for patient safety?

options.A: Patients prefer automated machines to human nursing care
options.B: Nurses refuse to report mistakes when watching patients closely
options.C: Technology is always more expensive than hiring extra staff
options.D: Human beings experience fatigue and burnout, which inevitably leads to errors

explanation: Even the best nurses get tired during long shifts. That's why we need reliable systems, not just sheer willpower! [learn more](GST319_U5_T4#GST319_U5_T4_h1)

question: What is a safe, effective substitute to enhance flavor without adding sodium?

options.A: Fresh garlic, ginger, and local herbs
options.B: Baking soda and chemical preservatives
options.C: Extra helpings of commercial seasoning cubes
options.D: Table salt mixed with white sugar

explanation: Aromatics like garlic and ginger provide strong flavors and aromas that compensate for a lack of salt. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h6)

question: What microscopic structures on the villi form the brush border of the small intestine?

options.A: Flagella
options.B: Sphincters
options.C: Microvilli
options.D: Cilia

explanation: Microvilli are tiny projections on the surface of intestinal absorptive cells that greatly increase surface area. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why is using strategic silence during an interview actually a great communication tool?

options.A: It shows the researcher is bored with the conversation
options.B: It gives the participant time to think and share deeper thoughts
options.C: It signals that the interview is officially over
options.D: It forces the participant to change the topic immediately

explanation: Spot on! Silence can feel awkward, but giving patients a moment to breathe lets them process deep emotions and share truly meaningful insights. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h5)

question: When doing an emergency primary survey (ABCDE), what do you check first?

options.A: Circulation
options.B: Disability
options.C: Exposure
options.D: Airway

explanation: Always start with 'A' for Airway! Making sure air can move freely into the lungs comes before anything else. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the main reason we write an incident report in the hospital?

options.A: To provide a permanent record for police investigations
options.B: To lower hospital insurance payments after a lawsuit
options.C: To gather evidence to sack a careless staff member
options.D: To document unexpected events and improve patient safety

explanation: Spot on! Incident reports are all about catching system errors so we can prevent them from happening again—not for witch-hunting or punishing staff. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h1)

question: What keeps urine from accidentally mixing with semen during ejaculation?

options.A: The prostate gland physically shrinks in size
options.B: Sperm cells actively push urine back into the kidneys
options.C: A sphincter muscle closes the bladder opening
options.D: The vas deferens ties off the urinary tubes

explanation: An internal urinary sphincter snaps shut tightly during ejaculation, ensuring that urine stays safely away from the semen. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T2#GNS121_U4_T2_h7)

question: A nurse needs a quick estimate of a patient's daily calorie needs without special gas-exchange equipment. What is best to use?

options.A: A validated predictive equation like the Mifflin-St Jeor formula
options.B: A laboratory blood test measuring thyroid antibody levels
options.C: A direct calorimetry thermal chamber room
options.D: A 24-hour continuous core body temperature recording

explanation: When fancy equipment isn't around, clinical formulas using age, weight, and height give us a fast, reliable estimate of calorie needs. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T9#GNS121_U1_T9_h3)

question: After a punch biopsy on the arm, a little blood keeps oozing out. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: Flush the open wound with sterile hydrogen peroxide
options.B: Remove the newly placed sutures to inspect the base
options.C: Apply direct firm pressure with sterile gauze
options.D: Immediately apply a full-thickness skin graft

explanation: Simple, direct pressure with sterile gauze is your best friend for stopping minor bleeding before doing anything else. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T3#GNS213_U5_T3_h5)

question: Why is wearing a medical alert bracelet so important for someone with hypoadrenalism?

options.A: It prevents the patient from developing secondary infections
options.B: It alerts emergency workers to their need for stress-dose steroids
options.C: It reminds the patient to take their daily morning pills
options.D: It measures blood sugar levels continuously throughout the day

explanation: If an emergency happens and the patient can't speak, the bracelet tells paramedics right away that they need life-saving steroids immediately. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T8#GNS211_U1_T8_h8)

question: How is the grey matter and white matter arranged inside the developing spinal cord?

options.A: White matter forms internally and gray matter forms externally
options.B: Sensory fibers are kept completely outside the spinal column
options.C: Gray matter forms internally and white matter forms externally
options.D: Motor neurons develop only within the outer white matter

explanation: Great thinking! The spinal cord is neatly organized with nerve cell bodies on the inside (grey matter) and nerve fiber tracts on the outside (white matter). [learn more](GNS211_U3_T1#GNS211_U3_T1_h4)
